raw_response:
I am a 57-year-old woman who has been farming these fields for 25 years. I never went to school, so I don't read books about farming, but I know my land. My family has 9.8 mu — not big, not small — just enough that we work hard and eat. My husband and my son both work off-farm at a factory in town, so during the busy times it's mostly me, though they come back for harvest and planting.

**Wheat**

The corn is almost ready to come off, and after that I'll plant wheat right away. I always plant wheat in the first half of October — if you plant too late, the wheat won't grow strong enough to survive the winter. I'll put wheat on all 9.8 mu, same as always. I buy my wheat seed from the seed shop in town, the kind everyone uses here. It costs about 30 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, last year I used two bags of compound fertilizer (that 15-15-15 kind) per mu as base fertilizer, and then at green-up time I put down another bag of urea per mu. That worked well — I got about 420 jin per mu. But fertilizer got more expensive this year, and my son says his factory hasn't been giving overtime. So I'm thinking maybe I'll cut back a little on the topdressing. I'll still put the compound fertilizer down at planting — about 15 kg per mu, that's three bags for the whole field. But for the spring topdressing, instead of a full bag of urea, maybe I'll do a bit less, maybe 10 kg per mu. If the wheat looks yellow and weak, I'll add more, but if it looks green, I'll save the money. Two bags of urea for the whole farm instead of three. The extension man says I should do more, but I know my soil — it's decent land, not the worst.

For irrigation, I'll water three times: once right after planting so the seeds sprout well, once in spring when it wakes up, and once at heading if it doesn't rain. Water costs money — every time I pump, the meter runs. Last year I watered four times and the bill was too high. Three should be enough if the winter snow is good.

Weeding — I'll spray herbicide once after planting. Everyone does it now, saves so much back-breaking work. If I see aphids in spring, I'll spray insecticide too.

**Maize**

After we harvest the wheat in early June, there's no time to rest. We have maybe five days to get the maize in the ground. I'll plant maize on all 9.8 mu. I usually buy hybrid seed — it's expensive, about 50 yuan per mu, but you get what you pay for. Last year I tried saving my own seed and the yield was terrible. Never again.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer at planting, about 15 kg per mu, and then at big flare stage I topdress with urea, about 10 kg per mu. The maize usually needs less fuss than wheat. I'll irrigate twice if it's dry — once at planting if there's no rain, and once at tasseling. If the summer rains are good, maybe only once. 

For labor, most of the work is me and my husband. During wheat harvest and maize planting in June, we hire two people for about three days because that week is impossible to do alone. That costs about 150 yuan per day per person. For wheat planting in October, I can manage with just family.

**My thinking**

I'm a bit worried about money this year. With my son's factory work uncertain, I want to keep some cash in my pocket. So I'm cutting back slightly on fertilizer and irrigation compared to last year — not much, just enough to feel safe. I'd rather have a little less yield than no money for medicine if someone gets sick. The land has been good to us for 25 years, it will forgive a small cut. I'll watch the wheat in spring — if it looks hungry, I'll feed it more, but I'll decide then, not now.
